newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: IMF says Ivory Coast economic reforms on course.
newsitem.headline: IMF says Ivory Coast economic reforms on course.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday that Ivory Coast's economic reforms are on course.

Amor Tahari, IMF director for Africa, said the world's top cocoa producer had made progress towards the growth and inflation targets set following the 1994 devaluation of the CFA franc used in much of French-speaking Africa.
"The program, put in place after the devaluation, has confirmed the progress Ivory Coast has made to achieve the growth and inflation control targets," he told reporters.
Tahari was visiting Ivory Coast at the head of an IMF mission which was reviewing progress half-way through a three-year Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility program.
An Ivorian team will head for Washington in November to prepare the ground for the final year of the program.
Ivorian Economy and Finance Minister N'Goran Niamien said June data suggested the agreed policies were working.
"The mid-term review, in other words the indicators at the end of June, show that state revenue is in line with forecasts; spending is under control, as is inflation," Niamien added.

After an economic boom following independence from France in 1960, Ivory Coast's economy slumped in the late 1980s. Gross domestic product grew 1.8 percent in 1994, heralding the start of a recovery. Growth in 1995 was 7.5. percent.
Inflation fell from 32 percent in 1994 to 7.7. percent in 1995, against a five percent target. The rate for 1996 thus far is 3.7 percent against a 4.9 percent target for the year.
